newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 lower Tuesday in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures drifted lower in sluggish trading today, with benchmark September briefly dipping below chart support at 1,000 stg a tonne. At the midday break, September was down 12 stg at 1,001 stg, traded 1,005 to 994 stg. December fell six stg to 1,038 stg.

Monday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly lower, pressured by late speculative liquidation. September settled down $17 at $1,500 per tonne after ranging between $1,527 and $1,495. Second-month December closed $18 lower at $1,546, with the back months down $17 to $19.
On the charts, traders said September has support near $1,490, with the next levels seen at $1,480 and $1,475. Resistance was pegged near the high of $1,527, followed by $1,540.
